## ✨ New Features

- **Issue a certificate now:** Request a new certificate before renewal is due, even when automatic management is disabled. Save your settings first; the button uses your saved staging/production and restart settings.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Issuance limits:** Manual requests retain the six-hour cooldown and certificate authority rate limits.

## ✨ New Features

- **Certificate issued date:** Show the certificate validity start date in your local time.
- **Repository link:** Open the GitHub repository from the top of the plugin configuration page.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Expired certificate status:** Resolved an issue where certificate status could remain outdated after expiration, including when automatic management was disabled.
- **Status messages:** Keep renewal errors visible and replace obsolete restart instructions.

## ✨ New Features

- **Certificate cleanup:** Retain replaced AutoCert certificates for five days after first observing them unused with the replacement active, then remove them at the next scheduled 12-hour check.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Protected certificates:** Keep the active production certificate, latest staging certificate, and externally supplied files. Cleanup waits for any pending restart.
- **Upgrade grace period:** Give existing old files a fresh five-day grace period when upgrading. Rollback to a deleted certificate is no longer available.
- **Stable release:** AutoCert 1.0.0.0 is now a regular release.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

versions.changelog: Fix: re-added missing Pocket ID preset and other small UI fixes

The hardened OIDC rewrite on Jellyfin 12. Hand-rolled OIDC flow with Trust-On-First-Use discovery-endpoint pinning and an SSRF-guarded, DNS-rebind-pinned HTTP client. Account identity keyed on the OIDC subject, in its own identity-map file (migrated out of the plugin config on upgrade). Fail-closed role-to-policy RBAC with a server-wide admission allowlist. OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0. Client-secret indirection (Client Secret File / ENV_VAR reference). Auto-managed SSO login button in Branding. Rewritten admin config page. Opt-in, per-provider verified-email account linking that never binds an administrator account. Username/email/display-name/email-verified now fall back to the userinfo endpoint when the ID token omits them. Token-validation failures surface a plain-language reason (expired cert, audience/issuer mismatch, clock drift, JWKS rotation) instead of a bare error. Fixed OIDC-authenticated sessions showing a blank IP in Jellyfin's activity log. Fixed the Manage Library Access checkbox not responding to clicks. No configuration migration required from 2.0.0.0. Renamed to SSO-OIDC-Authentication (was SSO-OIDC Authentication) so the install folder no longer mixes a space with a hyphen; your saved settings are unaffected.

BREAKING: requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer will not load on 10.10/10.11 (stay on 1.0.7.x for those). Retargeted to .NET 10 and rebuilt against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin API. Removed the vestigial IAuthenticationProvider.HasPassword override (dropped from the interface in 12.0). No functional changes to the OIDC login, RBAC, or Quick Connect flows.

Security: deny OIDC login when no RBAC role mapping (and no valid Default Role) matches the user's IdP roles, instead of silently letting login through with stale or default permissions — an intentional, unconditional fail-closed behavior change. Fix: declare style-src in the callback page's CSP and nonce the Quick Connect page's inline styles, closing a gap where that page was already CSP-non-compliant. Also: cosmetic redesign of the OIDC callback page (spinner, card layout, dark theme).

Security: evict stale entries from the rate limiter to prevent unbounded memory growth. Security: validate the OIDC picture-claim URL (scheme, host, redirects, size) before fetching it to prevent SSRF via a malicious/compromised IdP or self-service avatar. Security: block login/Quick Connect for a provider disabled mid-flow via an already-issued session token. Security: pin discovery and picture-fetch HTTP connections to the DNS-resolved address AuthorityGuard already validated, closing a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU gap. Also: OIDC callback page CSP now uses a per-response nonce instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

Fix: honor Jellyfin's Base URL setting in generated SSO links (login buttons, branding snippet, callback page) so they work behind a reverse-proxy base path. Feat: sign in native/mobile apps (Android, iOS/Swiftfin, Android TV) via a Quick Connect bridge, since the web login button doesn't reach them. Feat: sync the Jellyfin avatar from the IdP's picture claim on login, with a per-provider opt-out.

Feat: per-IP fixed-window rate limiting on OIDC auth endpoints. Fix: dead-code bug in ClaimParser where JSON array claim values were never parsed. CI: 77-test suite with AAA pattern coverage across all services and controllers.
Fix: role mappings added after a previous save were overwriting earlier ones. Rename plugin to SSO-OIDC Authentication.

versions.changelog: Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

Fixes a small but confusing moment with **Live TV** targets. Live TV has no posters to build a mosaic from, so the **Poster collage** background is unavailable there — and if you had already chosen a collage and then switched the target to Live TV, the background silently changed back to **Image** without a word. The option is now greyed out with a line explaining why, in all three languages, so the change no longer happens behind your back. Nothing else about how covers render has changed.

Adds **Spanish**. The whole configuration page — every step, label, button, hint and message, plus the server's upload and validation errors — is now translated, joining English and Dutch. The page follows your Jellyfin display language, and regional variants come along for the ride: `es-MX` and `es-419` get Spanish just like `es-ES`. Alongside it, the translation files themselves were **cleaned up and put under test**. Roughly a hundred strings left behind by the v3 editor rewrite were still being carried (and would have had to be translated into every new language) — those are gone, and five new build-time checks now fail if a language drifts out of sync with English, if a `{0}` placeholder goes missing, or if a string is defined but never shown. No change to how covers look or render.

Adds an **overlay gradient** to the Background step — a colour that fades in over your background and sits under your text. It is the missing piece behind the look where a poster **resolves into a solid band of colour** at the bottom, with the title on top of it and readable no matter what the poster shows underneath. Each colour stop has its own **opacity**, so you can go from fully transparent to fully solid, use **two colours** for a duotone fade, or wash the whole cover. Four **presets** — Bottom fade, Top fade, Full wash and Duotone — get you there in one click, and switching between them keeps the colours you have already picked so you can try all four without losing your palette. The **Auto palette** swatches now recolour the selected overlay stop, so you can tint a cover with a colour taken straight out of its own artwork. The overlay works with every background type — image, poster collage, gradient or solid — and with animated covers. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The configuration page is now a **guided walkthrough**. Instead of every control at once, designing a cover is laid out as five numbered steps — **Target**, **Background**, **Text & logos**, **Effects**, **Output** — with one open at a time and any of them one click away. Each step shows the controls most people need and keeps the rest under **Advanced**. Choosing a background is now a single choice — **image, poster collage, gradient or solid colour** — instead of a source dropdown plus a separate gradient tick that overlapped with it. The whole page is **properly usable on a phone**: bigger touch targets throughout, the preview pinned at the top while you work, a full-screen poster browser, and canvas handles you can actually grab (they used to shrink to a few pixels on a small screen). Two more additions: **undo and redo** across the whole design with Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, and an **in-context preview** showing your cover wide, square and poster-shaped before you apply it. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

Adds a new **Effects** card. A **colour wash** tints the background under your text, a **vignette** darkens the edges to draw the eye inward, **film grain** adds texture, and a **border** frames the cover — square or rounded, single or double-lined. Every effect is off until you switch it on, and turning one back down to zero leaves your cover exactly as it was. One click of **Jellyfin style** lays down the familiar dark-gradient look with clean white text, which you can then edit freely. And **Auto palette** reads the dominant colours straight out of your background and offers them as swatches — click one to recolour the selected text layer or the colour wash. Existing designs and saved templates are untouched and render exactly as before.

Covers are no longer one line of text. A new **Layers** card lets you stack **as many text layers as you like** plus your own **PNG logos and icons**, each independently styled and freely placed. Every layer can be **shown or hidden, reordered, duplicated, deleted** and selected from the list, and the card below it edits whichever layer you have selected. On the preview canvas, the selected layer gets **corner handles to resize it** and a **knob to rotate it** — hold **Shift** to keep a logo's proportions or snap rotation to 15°. Two new sliders, **Opacity** and **Rotation**, work on text and logos alike. Logos are uploaded the same way as backgrounds (PNG, transparency preserved) and are restored onto the canvas when you load a saved template. As always the server render stays authoritative, and rotated or faded text now renders there exactly as the preview shows it.

Fixes **Reposition background**, which barely worked in 3.0.0.0. Dragging the background now **follows your cursor exactly** — it used to lag badly at low zoom and overshoot at high zoom, matching the cursor only at one specific zoom level. More importantly, repositioning now **works straight away, without zooming in first**: on a **Fill** background you can slide a portrait poster up and down (or a wide still left and right) to choose which part of it the cover shows. Previously that did nothing at all until you zoomed in, because only the zoomed-in part of the image was treated as movable. The server render and the on-screen canvas were fixed together, so what you position is what gets applied. Designs you have already saved or applied are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The config page preview is now a **live interactive canvas**, not a static image: click the title to select it and **drag it** to position, and toggle **Reposition background** to **drag-pan** and **scroll/pinch-zoom** the background image directly on the canvas. A new **Show server render** button renders the exact same design on the server — the authoritative output, since the canvas is a fast approximation — so you can compare before applying. Designs are now stored internally in a new **layered document format** (title text is one layer, more layer types land in a later release); **existing saved templates migrate automatically** the first time you load them, so nothing is lost.

A code-quality and size pass. The plugin is now **much smaller** — the bundled Noto Sans fonts were subset to the glyphs cover titles use (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, punctuation), cutting the plugin DLL from ~3.9 MB to ~1.6 MB with no visible change. **Dead code was removed** (an unused retry service, an unused exceptions module, and nine internal API endpoints the UI never called), and the render pipeline was tidied up (the image compositing is no longer needlessly async). A few **security hardening** touches: the Apply and batch-apply endpoints are now rate-limited and batch size is capped, text size is clamped, poster-collage sources get the same decompression-bomb guard as other images, and error messages no longer echo server paths back to the browser. Purely internal — no user-facing behaviour changes.

Small UI fixes on the Target card: a **disabled button now clearly looks disabled** (dimmed, not-allowed cursor) — the Restore button no longer looks clickable when there's no backup yet — and the Restore row has proper spacing above it. Also added an animated preview to the README.

The **poster browser now covers every library type** — music albums and artists, books, music videos and photos, not just movies and shows — so you can pick a cover from a music or book library too. A **loading spinner** now shows over the preview while it renders, which helps for slower operations like building a poster collage. The **Apply** button now shows an "Applying…" state and locks while it works, so a slow render (like an animated GIF) no longer looks like nothing is happening. **Animated GIF covers are more reliable**: the working size is capped so a full-size render no longer takes forever or fails to apply, and text scales with it so the look is unchanged. The default **Landscape** size is now a lighter 1280×720 (it was 1920×1080) — plenty for library tiles and much smaller files; 1920 is still available via Custom. And the Templates and collage cards were tidied up — the **Delete** and **Shuffle** buttons now sit neatly next to their dropdowns instead of as oversized blocks.

Polish on the v2 release. The config page now matches Jellyfin more closely — compact colour pickers (they used to stretch the full width), and action buttons that align with the selects beside them. The preview no longer starts on a black canvas: it opens with Jellyfin's **brand gradient** (purple → blue) by default. And uploading an **animated GIF** as a background now animates the preview automatically — it switches to Animated GIF output and passes the source's frames through at their own timing, instead of showing a single still frame.

A big release. **Poster-collage backgrounds** build a grid mosaic from a target's own item posters (with density and shuffle controls). **Design templates** let you save a look and reuse it, and **batch apply** pushes one design onto many libraries, collections or playlists at once — each cover titled with its own target's name. **Animated GIF export** is now real: it passes through an animated-GIF background or applies a Ken Burns pan/zoom (capped at 30 frames). And **Restore original cover** reverts any target to its pre-plugin image — applying a cover now backs up the previous image automatically.

The plugin now has its own entry in the dashboard's left navigation menu, so you no longer have to open it through the Plugins list. Added **Live TV** as a cover target (best-effort — it sets the image on Jellyfin's generated Live TV view, which may not persist on every server). Moved the custom-font picker into the **Text** card where it belongs, and added a screenshot to the README.

Fixed the background dim: any non-zero dimming used to black out a picked poster entirely (JPEG posters have no alpha channel, so the overlay painted fully opaque). Dimming now composites correctly and the default was lowered to 0.25. Added an **Image fit** option — Fill (crop), Fit (show the whole image, letterboxed) or Stretch — so a portrait poster no longer gets cropped to a strip in a wide cover. New **multi-colour gradient** picker with an angle control for linear gradients and add/remove colour stops. You can now target **collections** and **playlists** in addition to libraries.

Poster background reliability: authenticate the image download, build the upload without the (sometimes unavailable) File constructor, and surface a clear message at each step so any failure is visible instead of silent.

Fixes. The config page now reliably follows your Jellyfin UI language — the detection reads Jellyfin's stored language setting, not just the browser language (Dutch now shows correctly). Picking a library poster as the background now works: the image is fetched through Jellyfin's own image endpoint and uploaded, instead of resolving a local file path that wasn't always available.

The config page now follows your Jellyfin UI language, with a complete Dutch (NL) translation and English fallback. Font weight now works — all six weights (Light–ExtraBold) are bundled as distinct Noto Sans faces. Background images are cover-fitted instead of stretched, so posters keep their aspect ratio. When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).

- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

name: Marquee Companion [✓✓✓]
description:
Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.

- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.

versions.changelog:
### Added

- A Quality column that names the class a frame falls in, from 144p to 8K, with an i in place of the p for interlaced video. It sorts by class rather than by how the name reads, and a filter picks a class from a list and holds rows at, above or below it. (#7)
- `Schema` answers the classes a quality can be held against, in their order.
- A failed export and a failed column save are reported in words of their own.

### Changed

- A CSV names the unit of a size, a runtime and a bitrate in its header. An ODS shows a runtime as a time, counted in hours past a day, and a size and a bitrate with their unit, all of them still numbers a spreadsheet can total. (#6)
- A number typed into a filter with the digit grouping the table prints is read as one number, so 48,000 is no longer 48.
- The README describes `search` and what an export holds, and names bytes per hour and truth values among the filter values.
- An advisory against a package Jellyfin brings along is a build warning rather than an error.

### Fixed

- The sidebar entry followed a language further down the browser's list when English came first, and could take one the browser had ruled out.
- A book ran for the second Jellyfin measures its reading progress in, and was given a size per hour from it.
- A series whose episodes run at 24000/1001 and at 2997/125 read as mixed in its frame rate, though every episode shows 23.976.
- A DVD or Blu-ray folder weighed only the first file of its title. It now weighs every file in the folder and shows no size per hour.
- A .strm took its bitrate and its size per hour from the bytes of the text file.
- The table kept its scroll position when a page turn, a sort, a search or a filter replaced its rows.
- A visit whose schema failed to load left an empty page behind, and a later one left the filter button disabled.
- Two quick changes to the rows per page or to the level a tab is expanded to could be stored in the wrong order.
- The spacing of the tab counts, the column picker and the row toggles did not follow a right-to-left layout.
- Three checks could not fail or skipped part of what they name: the rounded runtime of a series, the version in the README badge, and the names of the tabs.
- A failed library refresh ended the test run, a request the server never answered held it for good, and Ctrl-C waited for the helper container to finish.
- The fixture recipe of the screenshot script went on after a failed encode, and the version list did not retry a connection that dropped after the request was sent.

### Dependencies

- jsdom 30.1.1 in the tests. (#4)
- Renovate keeps `test/` in its scan through an empty `ignorePaths` rather than `ignorePresets`.

### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). # 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.
